title: Double crochet mesh table runner
subtitle: A filet-style cotton runner in double crochet and chain spaces
excerpt: A lightweight cotton table runner worked in a simple dc and chain-space mesh grid. The open mesh keeps the pattern light and lets the table surface show through. Cotton DK on a 4 mm hook.
sourceNotes: Open filet mesh is documented in Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776, filet crochet chapter. The dc-and-chain-space grid is the base construction of all filet work.

glossaryTerms.definition: A style of crochet using a regular grid of filled and empty squares, typically worked in trebles and chain spaces, to create patterns or pictorial motifs.

content.text: A double crochet mesh table runner is a 30 × 120 cm cotton strip worked in
filet crochet

: a regular open-mesh grid of double crochets and two-chain spaces. The result is lightweight enough to layer over a tablecloth or use alone on a bare table; the mesh allows the surface underneath to show. Works in any DK cotton; a neutral colour or a natural undyed cotton suits most tables.

The runner is worked flat, back and forth, in rows. Each row starts with ch 5 (counts as first tr + ch 2) and ends with a tr into the last dc of the previous row. Block the finished runner wet for a flat, even mesh: cotton relaxes and the mesh squares become regular.
Materials
200 m DK cotton (100% cotton or linen-cotton blend). Two 100 m balls cover one runner in a single colour.
Gauge
One mesh unit (1 dc + ch 2 + 1 dc) = 1.5 cm wide in DK cotton with a 4 mm hook, blocked. 8 rows = 10 cm tall, blocked. Work a 10-unit × 8-row swatch to check width and height before starting.
Stitches used
Chain (ch)
Slip stitch (sl st)
Double crochet (dc). UK term; US equivalent is single crochet (sc)
Treble (tr). UK term; US equivalent is double crochet (dc). Used only for the turning chain edge stitches.
Pattern
Foundation
Ch 63. (The foundation chain is a multiple of 3 plus 3 for the turning chain. 63 ch = 20 mesh units wide.)
Row 1 (right side)
1 tr into 6th ch from hook (counts as tr + ch 2 space), *ch 2, skip 2 ch, 1 tr into next ch; repeat from * to end (20 tr + 19 ch-2 spaces = 20 mesh units). Turn.
Row 2 and every following row
Ch 5 (counts as tr + ch 2). *1 tr into next tr, ch 2; repeat from * across, ending 1 tr into top of turning ch. Turn. (20 mesh units per row.)
Work rows until the runner measures 120 cm from the foundation chain, ending with a right-side row. At the stated gauge, this is approximately 96 rows. Fasten off.
Edging (optional)
Work one round of dc evenly around all four edges, with 3 dc into each corner. Sl st to join. Fasten off. The edging firms up the perimeter and keeps the mesh from rolling at the edges.
Finishing

Weave in both ends. Wet-block the runner by submerging in cool water, squeezing gently, then pinning to size on a blocking mat. Pin the long edges straight and the short ends square. Leave until completely dry: usually several hours. The mesh squares become regular and the runner lies flat after blocking.
Care
Machine-wash on a 30°C gentle cycle. Reshape and dry flat, or re-pin if needed after heavy washing.
